Festive demand drives M&M vehicle sales to an all-time high in Oct
articles.summary:
Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd on Sunday said its total vehicle sales grew 9 per cent year-on-year to a record 13,1109 units in October.
The total sales include exports, which rose 77 per cent to 7,102 units during the month.
Mahindra & Mahindra said domestic passenger vehicle sales rose 2 per cent year-on-year to 73,338 units in October, and commercial vehicle sales rose 4 per cent to 33,037 units.
M&M Automotive business President Velusamy R said the company's SUV sales of 73,338 units and total vehicle sales of 13,1109 units in October were the highest ever in any month.
The festive season, together with a refreshed portfolio, kept demand strong across SUVs, pick-ups and three-wheelers. Our first CNG vehicle, the XUV 3XO ZNG, has also seen strong traction with customers, he said.
In commercial vehicles, three-wheeler sales, including electric ones, increased 38 per cent to 17,632 units. LCVs between 2-3.5 ton grew 5 per cent to 28,654 units, while sales of LCVs under 2 ton ...

Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd on Sunday said its total vehicle sales grew 9 per cent year-on-year to a record 13,1109 units in October.
The total sales include exports, which rose 77 per cent to 7,102 units during the month.
Mahindra & Mahindra said domestic passenger vehicle sales rose 2 per cent year-on-year to 73,338 units in October, and commercial vehicle sales rose 4 per cent to 33,037 units.
M&M Automotive business President Velusamy R said the company's SUV sales of 73,338 units and total vehicle sales of 13,1109 units in October were the highest ever in any month.
The festive season, together with a refreshed portfolio, kept demand strong across SUVs, pick-ups and three-wheelers. Our first CNG vehicle, the XUV 3XO ZNG, has also seen strong traction with customers, he said.

Chairman’s
Letter




                                                    Bifocal Vision
                                                    Embracing the past.
                                                   Envisioning the future.
The Lion Capital, Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, c.1905
 In the heart of Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, stands the illustrious Lion Capital, a tribute to Ashoka’s Mauryan dynasty from the third
century BC. Crafted from gleaming sandstone, it depicts four lions regally seated atop an abacus, and today, this relic is enshrined
in the sanctity of the Sarnath Museum. As India stepped into its republic era on January 26, 1950, this artifact, steeped in heritage,
was chosen as our National Emblem, symbolising India’s strength, unity, and undying legacy. Its depiction on our currency is
a poignant reminder of our deep historical roots. Yet, as India strides into the digital age, pioneering in sectors like financial
inclusivity and modernised payments, the Reserve Bank of India’s unveiling of the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) signifies a
harmonious blend of our ancient ethos with modern innovation. Just as the emblematic lions stand sentinel across ages, the CBDC
connects our revered past with a transformative financial horizon.
    Chairman’s Letter                                                                                            Annual Report 2022-23




Chairman’s Letter
FY23 was a year of whirlwind change and challenges for the global economy. We witnessed a
series of significant events, starting with a global economic revival and the return to complete
normalcy after recovering from the pandemic. This gave the world a glimmer of hope for a strong
fiscal year ahead. However, this uptick remained short-lived and was overshadowed by the
economic volatility that has characterised much of this fiscal period.


The Year Gone by –
Volatility, War, Inflation and an Inverted Yield Curve

The global economic landscape experienced unprecedented volatility during FY23. The year began with the rallying of the US dollar
to an all-time high, only to reverse all its gains by the end of the fiscal year. Gold prices reached record levels, bond yields remained
elevated, and the yield curve was inverted. Most major advanced economies showed signs of a looming recession, with significant
concerns over the Eurozone.

Amidst all these challenges in the global scenario, India emerged as a bright spot. According to World Bank’s report, India’s
growth continues to be resilient despite macroeconomic headwinds and the country remains largely unaffected by the global
environment. This decoupling can in parts be attributed to our local demand cycle which displays a slightly different cadence from
global demand. During the year, India’s composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) reached a 13-year high, Consumer Price Index
(CPI) touched an 18-month low and Wholesale Price Index (WPI) hit a 3-year low. The 10-year Government Securities yield has fallen
below 7% after 13 months and Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections recorded the highest monthly collection in April.

India also entered the league of the top five global economies surpassing the United Kingdom and has defied all odds to become
the fastest growing economy: a matter of immense pride for all of us. I can say that in my long career I have not seen a better
economic environment in India as we are seeing now - A new dawn is on the horizon as India enters its Amrit Kaal, and is poised to
become Vishwaguru.




                           I can say that in my long career I have not seen a better
                           economic environment in India as we are seeing now -
                           India is poised for growth.

Bajaj Auto's total sales during October rise 14% to 591,876 units
articles.summary:
Bajaj Auto on Monday posted a 14 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October, with double-digit growth across two-wheelers and commercial vehicles.
The automaker's total wholesales stood at 5,91,876 units, against 5,18,170 units in the year-ago period, according to an exchange filing.
Domestic sales rose 12 per cent to 3,51,148 units, while exports grew 18 per cent to 2,40,728 units.
Total two-wheeler sales increased by 13 per cent to 5,01,194 units from 4,42,316 in the year-ago period.
Total commercial vehicle sales were higher by 20 per cent to 90,682 units, compared to 75,854 units.
Bajaj Auto's total sales during the April-October period rose 22 per cent to 35,79,011 units.
Two-wheeler sales rose 22 per cent to 30,07,707 units, while commercial vehicle sales were higher by 23 per cent at 5,71,304 units.

articles.summary:
Realty firm Puravankara Ltd has reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 83.74 crore for the quarter ended September on higher revenue. Bengaluru-based Puravankara Ltd had posted a net loss of Rs 42.99 crore in the year-ago period.
Total income rose to Rs 1,051.02 crore in the second quarter of this fiscal, from Rs 662.73 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding year, according to a regulatory filing.
During the first half of this fiscal, the company posted a net profit of Rs 107.24 crore as against a net loss of Rs 111.42 crore in the year-ago period.
Total income surged to Rs 1,928.17 crore in the April-September period of 2026-27 fiscal from Rs 1,201.37 crore in the corresponding period of the preceding year.

articles.summary:
Bajaj Auto on Monday posted a 14 per cent year-on-year growth in its total sales during October, with double-digit growth across two-wheelers and commercial vehicles.
The automaker's total wholesales stood at 5,91,876 units, against 5,18,170 units in the year-ago period, according to an exchange filing.
Domestic sales rose 12 per cent to 3,51,148 units, while exports grew 18 per cent to 2,40,728 units.
Total two-wheeler sales increased by 13 per cent to 5,01,194 units from 4,42,316 in the year-ago period.
Total commercial vehicle sales were higher by 20 per cent to 90,682 units, compared to 75,854 units.
Bajaj Auto's total sales during the April-October period rose 22 per cent to 35,79,011 units.
Two-wheeler sales rose 22 per cent to 30,07,707 units, while commercial vehicle sales were higher by 23 per cent at 5,71,304 units.
